tests.title: The landing page describes the service and offers sign-in
given: a visitor with no session
tests.when: the service's root page is opened
then: the page is served successfully
it carries a description of the service
it carries a sign-in control that leads to the provider
tests.pseudocode: in the landing page test file: r = render('/'); assert r.ok and r.text contains the description and a sign-in control

tests.title: An unauthenticated visitor is told nothing about the deployment
given: a deployment holding workspaces, users and organizations with distinctive names
tests.when: every page reachable without a session is fetched, including the landing page and the addresses of the dashboard and a workspace view
then: no response contains any workspace slug, user name or organization name
no response contains a count of them
tests.pseudocode: in the web smoke-adjacent integration test file: for page in public_pages(): assert no SENTINEL names in page.text

tests.title: Signing in establishes a session for the right user
given: a stub OAuth provider and two users with different workspaces
tests.when: each signs in through the web interface and opens the dashboard
then: each session identifies the user the provider authenticated
each dashboard shows that user's workspaces and not the other's
tests.pseudocode: in the web session integration test file: s = sign_in(userA); assert slugs(dashboard(s)) == workspaces_of(userA)

tests.title: A browser sign-in leaves the person's API keys alone
given: a user holding two live API keys and a personal access token
tests.when: the user signs in through the web interface and the credentials are then used and listed
then: both API keys are still accepted by the API
the token is still accepted
the user's key list is unchanged and no new key was created
tests.pseudocode: in the web session integration test file: before = keys(user); sign_in_web(user); assert keys(user) == before and call(keyA).status == 200

tests.title: A session cannot be replayed, outlives nothing and ends on sign-out
given: a signed-in person, a controllable clock and a request originating from another site
tests.when: a cross-site request is made with no deliberate credential, the clock is advanced past the session's lifetime, and the person signs out and the old session value is reused
then: the cross-site request is not served as that person
the expired session is not accepted
the signed-out session value is refused
tests.pseudocode: in the web session integration test file, table over the three cases asserting the request is not served as the user

tests.title: A missing or dead session shows the landing page
given: no session, an expired session and a signed-out session
tests.when: the dashboard and a workspace view are opened with each
then: each shows the landing page with its sign-in control
no error page or stack trace is shown
tests.pseudocode: in the web session test file, table over (sessionState, page) asserting the landing page is rendered

tests.title: The dashboard lists workspaces with their four fields and links
given: a signed-in person with three workspaces at different statuses and access levels, one never synced
tests.when: the dashboard is opened
then: each workspace appears once with its slug, status, the person's access and its last sync
the never-synced workspace shows that it has not synced rather than an empty cell
each row links to that workspace's view and the link resolves
tests.pseudocode: in the dashboard integration test file: d = render(dashboard, session); assert rows(d) have the four fields and each link resolves

tests.title: The dashboard lists exactly what the API would
given: a person owning two workspaces, a member of an organization owning one more, and two workspaces belonging to neither
tests.when: the dashboard is opened and the API's workspace list is read with the same person's credential
then: the set of slugs shown equals the set the API returns
neither unrelated workspace appears
tests.pseudocode: in the dashboard integration test file: assert set(slugs(dashboard(session))) == set(slugs(api_list(user)))

tests.title: A person with no workspaces is told so
given: a signed-in person with no workspaces
tests.when: the dashboard is opened
then: the page carries a message saying there are no workspaces yet and what to do next
it is not an empty list with no explanation
tests.pseudocode: in the dashboard test file: assert 'no workspaces' in render(dashboard, emptyUser).text

tests.title: The workspace view shows the workspace's fields
given: a ready workspace with a description and settings, a failed one with a clone error, and one with a sync error
tests.when: each is opened
then: the slug, display name, description, status, mode, head, upstream head, last sync and settings are shown with the API's values
the clone error and the sync error are shown where set
an error field that is null is not shown
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace view integration test file, table over the three workspaces asserting the rendered fields against the API's response

tests.title: A carry-patch workspace shows its patches and latest rebuild
given: a carry_patch workspace with four patches at different statuses and a completed rebuild, one with no rebuild yet, and a standard workspace
tests.when: each is opened
then: the patches appear in ascending position order with position, branch, status and latest rebuild result
the latest rebuild's status is shown, or a statement that none has run
the standard workspace shows no patch section
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace view integration test file: assert [p.position for p in patches(view)] == [1,2,3,4] and 'no rebuild' in view_without_rebuild.text

tests.title: The workspace view shows recent jobs and events
given: a workspace with several merge and rebuild jobs and a dozen recorded events
tests.when: the workspace view is opened
then: the most recent jobs the API returns are shown, newest first, each with its kind and time
the most recent events are shown, newest first, each with its kind and time
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace view integration test file: assert [e.time for e in events(view)] == sorted(..., reverse=True)

tests.title: One failing section leaves the rest of the page usable
given: a workspace whose patch read, whose job read and whose event read fail in turn
tests.when: the workspace view is opened in each case
then: the other sections render with their data
the failing section carries a message naming what could not be read
the page is served rather than failing as a whole
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace view integration test file, table over the failing sections asserting the others rendered and a named message

tests.title: Every page reads through the API as the signed-in person
given: a recording API layer and recording store clients
tests.when: the dashboard and a workspace view are rendered for a signed-in person
then: every datum shown corresponds to a response the API returned for that person
no page read the relational store or the repository store directly
tests.pseudocode: in the web reads integration test file: render(views); assert store.directReads == 0 and api.calls were all made as the session's user

tests.title: A workspace the person may not read cannot be opened by address
given: a workspace belonging to someone else, an archived one they may not see, and an address naming no workspace
tests.when: each address is opened by a signed-in person
then: each page says the workspace is not available
none shows any field of a workspace
the three answers are indistinguishable
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace view test file: assert render(foreign).text == render(unknown).text and no workspace fields are present

tests.title: A member sees the member's view
given: a workspace, its owner and a member of its organization
tests.when: both open the workspace view
then: the member sees the fields the API returns them
every section the API would refuse the member is absent from their page
the member's access is shown as member
tests.pseudocode: in the workspace view integration test file: assert sections(view(member)) <= sections(view(owner)) and view(member).access == 'member'

tests.title: The pages use the shared design tokens and patterns
given: the rendered landing page, dashboard and workspace view
tests.when: each is inspected for its components and its type and spacing values
then: the dashboard uses the repository-list pattern, a workspace's status uses the status-badge pattern and the events use the timeline pattern
every type and spacing value comes from the project's design tokens rather than a literal
the same token set is used by all three pages
tests.pseudocode: in the design system test file: assert uses_pattern(dashboard, 'repo-list') and no hard-coded font sizes or spacings appear in the rendered styles

tests.title: Both themes render and meet the contrast level
given: every page, rendered with the system setting dark, with it light, and with an explicit override of each
tests.when: each rendering is inspected and its text and background pairs measured
then: every page renders in both themes
the theme follows the system setting by default and an explicit choice is remembered across a reload
every text and background pair meets the contrast level for normal text in both themes
tests.pseudocode: in the theming integration test file: for page, theme in product(PAGES, THEMES): assert min_contrast(render(page, theme)) >= NORMAL_TEXT_LEVEL

tests.title: Every page works at a phone's width
given: every page, rendered at a viewport 360 pixels wide, with both a short and a long workspace slug and a long description
tests.when: each rendering is measured
then: no page scrolls horizontally
no content is clipped or overlapping
the long slug and description wrap rather than widening the page
tests.pseudocode: in the responsive integration test file: for page in PAGES: r = render(page, width=360); assert r.scrollWidth <= 360 and no overlaps

tests.title: Every page is operable from the keyboard and announced correctly
given: every page with its interactive elements
tests.when: each is traversed by keyboard and inspected for structure and names
then: every link, button and control is reachable in a sensible order and can be activated from the keyboard
each focused element shows a visible focus indicator
each page has one main landmark and a heading structure with no skipped level
every control has an accessible name
tests.pseudocode: in the accessibility integration test file: for page in PAGES: assert tab_order_covers_all_controls(page) and one_main_landmark(page) and no_skipped_heading_levels(page)

tests.title: The interface is Parley's and does not present itself as GitHub
given: every page in both themes
tests.when: each is inspected for names, marks and claims
then: every page carries Parley's name
no page uses GitHub's name, logo or wordmark as its own identity
no page claims or implies an association with GitHub
tests.pseudocode: in the branding test file: for page in PAGES: assert 'Parley' in page.text and no GitHub mark is used as the site identity

tests.title: A developer signs in and their agent's key keeps working
given: a running deployment with the web interface served, a stub OAuth provider, and a user holding a live API key
tests.when: a browser opens the landing page, signs in, lands on the dashboard, and the API key is then used
then: the dashboard shows that user's workspaces
the API key is still accepted
the user's key list is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the web smoke test file, driving a real browser against a running deployment: open('/'); sign_in(); assert dashboard_visible(); assert call(apiKey).status == 200

tests.title: A developer reads a patch stack's health in the browser
given: a running deployment, a signed-in developer and a carry_patch workspace with patches, a completed rebuild, recent jobs and recent events
tests.when: the developer opens the workspace from the dashboard
then: the workspace's state, its patches with their latest rebuild results, the latest rebuild and the recent events are all on the page
the values match what the API returns for that person
the page renders in the viewer's theme at a phone's width
tests.pseudocode: in the web smoke test file: open(dashboard); click(workspace); assert patches_visible() and latest_rebuild_visible() and events_visible()

tests.title: A member sees their organization's workspaces and nothing else
given: a running deployment, a person who is a member of an organization with one workspace and owns another, and a third workspace they may not read
tests.when: the person signs in, reads the dashboard, opens the organization's workspace, and then types the address of the third
then: the dashboard lists their own and the organization's workspaces and not the third
the organization's workspace opens with the member's view
the third's address says it is not available and shows none of its fields
tests.pseudocode: in the web smoke test file: assert slugs(dashboard) == {own, orgWs}; open(orgWs); assert access_shown == 'member'; open(foreign); assert not_available()
